name: Analytical Gradients
text:
# Analytical Gradients
## Overview
Analytical gradients compute exact derivatives of the rendering equation with respect to input parameters by differentiating the continuous mathematical operations of the rendering pipeline, rather than relying on finite differences or reverse-mode [automatic differentiation](#7151-automatic-differentiation-reverse-adjoint-mode.md) [S1, unofficial]. This family solves the problem of high memory consumption and computational overhead associated with backpropagating gradients through long, discrete computational graphs [S5]. It sets itself apart from [Differentiable volume rendering](43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md) alternatives like [Automatic Differentiation (Reverse/Adjoint Mode)](7151-automatic-differentiation-reverse-adjoint-mode.md) by providing closed-form expressions that reduce memory usage to $O(n)$ and avoid the accumulation of numerical noise [S5].
## Shared principles
The family shares the principle of explicit differentiation of the rendering integral or projection operator. For a rendering function $F(\mathbf{x})$, where $\mathbf{x}$ represents parameters (e.g., density, geometry, camera), the gradient $\nabla_{\mathbf{x}} F$ is derived analytically. This requires the rendering operation to be differentiable almost everywhere, excluding discrete steps such as triangle selection or ray-casting branch decisions [S1, unofficial]. The gradients are computed by applying the chain rule to the continuous components (e.g., interpolation, integration, projection) [G].
## Subtopics

### [Differentiable Volume Rendering via Box Splines](2449-differentiable-volume-rendering-via-box-splines.md)
Computes the [differentiable X-ray transform](#2449-differentiable-volume-rendering-via-box-splines.md) of a volume using box spline interpolation. It provides exact gradients with respect to ray parameters (origin $\mathbf{t}$, direction $\mathbf{n}$) and volume coefficients. Choose this for tomography and geometry calibration where ray-traced geometry gradients are critical. It differs from siblings by explicitly computing adjoint functions for ray parameters while using standard adjoint transforms for volume coefficients.

### [Differentiable Volume Rendering with Analytical Gradients](5983-differentiable-volume-rendering-with-analytical-gradients.md)
Computes radiance and its analytical derivatives with respect to volume density directly. Choose this when avoiding the overhead of propagating gradients through long computational graphs inherent in automatic differentiation is required. It sets itself apart by focusing on direct density gradients in volumetric fields.

### [Analytical Derivative of Rendering (Mesh)](6761-analytical-derivative-of-rendering-mesh.md)
Computes exact gradients for explicit polygonal meshes by differentiating continuous steps (projection, interpolation) while excluding discrete triangle selection. Choose this for mesh-based inverse rendering. It differs from siblings by operating on [barycentric interpolation](#9603-barycentric-interpolation.md) and rasterization logic rather than volumetric fields.

## Background
The concept originates from the need to optimize differentiable rendering pipelines efficiently. While [reverse-mode AD](#789-adjoint-method.md) is standard, it scales poorly with the number of samples [S5]. Analytical approaches were developed to provide memory-efficient alternatives for specific rendering primitives, such as volume rendering [S1, unofficial] and mesh rasterization [S1, unofficial].
